about.title: Eureka Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Eureka's collisions often cluster along Broadway Street, Highway 101, H Street, and I Street, especially as Friday commute traffic builds toward the evening hours. With 214 injury collisions and 288 people hurt in the most recent reporting year, many Humboldt County residents find themselves suddenly dealing with medical bills, missed work, and an insurance adjuster who calls before the dust has settled. LawProactive isn't a law firm — we're a free service that connects injured Eureka drivers, passengers, cyclists, and pedestrians with independent personal injury attorneys who work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you. Because evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, and witness memories fade quickly, getting matched with an attorney soon after your crash can make a real difference in how your claim is built and supported.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Deadline Is Closer Than It Feels
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a claim, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — like the City of Eureka or Caltrans — may be responsible. Missing that shorter deadline can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce What You Receive
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by whatever percentage you're found responsible for. An attorney can help make sure the insurance company doesn't unfairly shift blame onto you.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California doesn't limit compensation for pain, suffering, and other non-economic losses in most car accident cases. That makes it especially important to document the full impact of your injuries, not just medical bills.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid recorded statements until you've spoken with an attorney. Insurers often use recorded answers, even innocent ones, to minimize or deny claims later. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to share.

items.question: What if my accident happened at a Eureka intersection with unclear fault?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover compensation even if you were partly at fault, though your amount may be reduced. An attorney can help gather evidence — witness statements, traffic camera footage, or police reports — to establish what actually happened.

items.question: How much does it cost to work with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: LawProactive's matching service is completely free, and independent attorneys in our network work on contingency. That means you pay nothing upfront, and there's no fee unless the attorney recovers money on your behalf.
